strategy: Analyze reference video with CV2, extract orbital parameters, build MoviePy scene from math models
agent_behavior: Extracted 8 sample frames from reference.mp4 using ffmpeg and visually inspected them to understand the animation structure
Wrote Python analysis scripts using OpenCV to detect colored blobs (sun, 6 planets) by HSV color ranges and tracked positions across all 360 frames
Fitted elliptical orbits to each planet's trajectory using SVD-based conic fitting, determining semi-axes and tilt angles
Discovered four animation phases: baseline orbits, linear radius expansion, peak orbits, and shrinking with reversed/accelerating angular velocity
Identified orbit ring dots (faint background markers at radii 60/80/100/120) through pixel brightness analysis
Built scene.py using MoviePy VideoClip with numpy frame generation and cv2 circle drawing, implementing the 4-phase orbital model
Added sub-pixel rendering using cv2 shift parameter for smoother planet edges, though this slightly increased mean diff
Performed iterative comparison against reference using per-frame mean pixel difference, achieving ~1.65 average diff
